- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) or shows sharp reversal, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for sentiment-driven rebound.  
- Model consistently overpredicts prices after recent spikes (e.g., >75.00), especially if sentiment was neutral or slightly negative — apply downward correction of 2–5% for 2–3 periods post-spike.  
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >5% deviation) and sentiment is flat or mildly positive, assume mean reversion; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 periods.  
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome (e.g., <3% deviation) and sentiment is positive, consider “sentiment lag” — forecast may be too conservative; add 0.5–1.5% to next period.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses short-term volatility — if sentiment shifts sharply within 5 days, adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in sentiment impact.
